stories.h: After 20 years of marriage, Kwankwaso's daughter Zainab files for divorce from Kano Governor Abba Yusuf, offers to refund dowry
stories.p: Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, daughter of Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, has reportedly filed for divorce from her husband, Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, at an Upper Area Court in Abuja, and offered to refund her dowry. The governor has been summoned to appear on 17 November.
body: Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, daughter of former Kano governor and senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has reportedly filed for divorce from her husband, Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, after 20 years of marriage.
## The court case
The case was filed at the Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja. A civil summons directs Governor Yusuf to appear in court on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.
Zainab is reported to be seeking khul'i, a process under Islamic law that allows a wife to end her marriage, and has offered to refund the dowry Yusuf paid when they married.
The summons is not a divorce order, and the court has yet to rule on the matter.
## Her reasons
According to the filing, Zainab cited a long absence of mutual care, love and emotional connection in the marriage, and said reconciliation efforts had failed.
The couple married on 29 July 2006, when Zainab was working as an aide to her father, who was then governor of Kano State. They have six children.
## The political backdrop
The marriage once symbolised the close bond between Kwankwaso and Yusuf, his long-time political protégé. That relationship has since broken down.
In January 2026, Governor Yusuf left Kwankwaso's party, the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), a move Kwankwaso's camp described as a betrayal.
Some reports have linked the political split to tension in the marriage, but the reasons given in the court filing focus on the breakdown of the relationship itself.
## No comment yet
As of Saturday, neither Governor Yusuf, Zainab nor Senator Kwankwaso had made a public statement on the divorce, and the Kano State Government had not commented.
## Over to you
Did politics cost this 20-year marriage, or is this simply a private family matter that should be left to the court?
more: Zainab Kwankwaso filed for divorce at an Abuja Upper Area Court.
She offered to refund her dowry under khul'i.

stories.h: Ronaldinho makes winning comeback at 46 as Ravenna beat Forli
stories.p: Brazilian legend Ronaldinho is set to start for Serie C club Ravenna against Forli on Sunday, his first competitive match in more than a decade, the club's manager has confirmed.
body: Former Barcelona, PSG and AC Milan star Ronaldinho is set to return to competitive football at the age of 46.
## The comeback

Ravenna manager Andrea Mandorlini confirmed on Friday, 13 November 2026, that the Brazilian will start for the Italian Serie C club in a local derby against Forli on Sunday, 15 November, as one of three forwards. Mandorlini described him as one of the greatest players of the modern era, adding that the coaching staff would decide together how long he plays.
## A long wait
Ronaldinho joined Ravenna as an investor in August. His last competitive appearance was for Brazilian club Fluminense in September 2015, making Sunday's match his first in more than ten years.
## Background
Ronaldinho won the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and the World Cup with Brazil in 2002, and is remembered as one of the most gifted and entertaining players of his generation.
## The comeback

Ronaldinho played the first half as Ravenna beat Forli 2-0 on Sunday, 15 November, in front of a packed crowd at the Stadio Bruno Benelli, where the club had installed a temporary 1,800-seat stand for the occasion. He walked out to flares and music, and although he played at a relaxed pace and mostly made simple passes, he was involved in the move that led to one of the goals.

stories.h: Kano drug task force seals pharmaceutical company after major pregabalin seizure
stories.p: The Kano State Multi-Agency Task Force on Drug Abuse has sealed a pharmaceutical company after recovering about 3.18 million capsules suspected to be pregabalin, worth more than ₦900 million. Allegations of regulatory failures are still under investigation.
body: The Kano State Multi-Agency Task Force on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking has sealed a pharmaceutical company following the earlier recovery of about 3.18 million capsules suspected to be pregabalin.
## A ₦900 million haul
The task force estimates the value of the seized stock at more than ₦900 million. Photos of the seizure show cartons packed with boxes and blister packs of red-and-white capsules.

Pregabalin is a prescription medicine used to treat nerve pain and some other conditions. It is widely misused in parts of northern Nigeria, where it is taken in large doses for its sedating effects, and is a growing concern for health and security authorities.
## Questions for the regulators
The task force has also raised allegations of possible regulatory failures that may have allowed such a large quantity of the drug to circulate.
The Pharmacists Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) had not responded to the allegations at the time of reporting.
## What is confirmed
The sealing of the company is confirmed. The allegations against the company and against regulatory officials remain under investigation and should not be treated as established facts.
## Over to you
How could controlled medicines reach illegal distribution networks on this scale, and what should regulators do to stop it?

stories.p: Campaigning in Bauchi, ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar said the Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria has lost close to 40 per cent of its members in two years, blaming soaring energy and financing costs under President Tinubu.
body: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Tinubu administration of pushing Nigeria's baking industry to the brink.
## What he said

In a statement released in Bauchi on Saturday, 14 November 2026, by Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication for his campaign, Atiku said the Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria had lost close to 40 per cent of its members in two years. He was in the state as part of what his campaign calls its 'affordable life' tour.

According to the statement, energy accounts for roughly half of most bakeries' production costs. It said one operator's monthly diesel bill had risen from ₦9 million to ₦19 million, and that switching to alternative power could cost a small bakery ₦40 million to ₦50 million, money most cannot raise. The statement blamed high energy prices and expensive financing for the closures.
## Bakers confirm

The Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria itself said at an exhibition in Lagos that about 40 per cent of its members had shut down in the past two years because of rising energy costs, expensive loans and economic conditions. Its president, Emmanuel Onuorah, called on the federal government to provide grants and single-digit interest loans to businesses in the real sector, warning that more closures could threaten jobs.
## Background

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has made the cost of living a central theme of his campaign. The government says its reforms, including the removal of fuel subsidy, were necessary to stabilise the economy and free up money for infrastructure. The Presidency had not responded to the statement at the time of writing. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.

Atiku launched the North-East leg of his campaign in Bauchi on 14 November, holding stakeholder meetings and a rally that his campaign said drew a large crowd, and promised to carry his message of affordable living across the country.

stories.h: When Congo turned on Lumumba, Egypt did not abandon his family: how Nasser sent a colonel to save his children
stories.p: As Patrice Lumumba's government collapsed and his life came under threat, Egypt's President Gamal Abdel Nasser ordered a secret mission led by Colonel Saad El-Din El-Shazly to get Lumumba's children out of Congo. They grew up in Cairo under Egypt's protection.
body: It is one of the lesser-known chapters of Africa's liberation story, and a remarkable act of solidarity between two African nations.
## A leader in danger

Patrice Lumumba, Congo's first Prime Minister after independence from Belgium in 1960, was overthrown within months and placed under house arrest. In January 1961 he was handed over to his enemies and assassinated, one of the most shocking political killings in African history.
As Congo descended into chaos, Lumumba's family was in grave danger, and his wife Pauline and their children had nowhere safe to turn.
## Nasser's secret mission

Egypt did not look away. On the direct orders of President Gamal Abdel Nasser, Colonel Saad El-Din El-Shazly, who later became one of Egypt's most celebrated military commanders, took on the task of getting Lumumba's children safely out of the country.
El-Shazly knew Congo well. He had commanded the Egyptian battalion sent there in 1960 as part of the international force during the independence crisis, at a time when Egypt firmly backed Lumumba.

The operation was carried out in complete secrecy. Lumumba's children, including his eldest son François, were smuggled out of Congo and flown to Cairo, where they arrived safely while their father was still under arrest.
## A new home in Cairo
After Lumumba's death, Pauline joined the children in Egypt. Nasser offered the family protection and support, and the Egyptian government helped with their housing, schooling and other needs.
Lumumba's children grew up in Egypt, which became not just a place of refuge but a home that embraced their father's cause as a symbol of African liberation.
Pauline later spent time in Europe before returning to Congo in the late 1960s, after Lumumba began to be honoured as a national hero. She settled in Kinshasa.
## Africa looking out for its own

The story is a reminder that Egypt was not just a witness to Africa's independence struggles, but an active partner in them. When Lumumba's family was in danger, an African nation stepped in to protect them.
## Over to you
Did you know this part of Lumumba's story? What does it tell us about African solidarity then, and now?
more: Nasser ordered Lumumba's children to be secretly evacuated.
Colonel Saad El-Din El-Shazly led the mission.
The family lived in Cairo under Egypt's protection.

stories.h: Nigerian-American ex-police officer Sinmi Asomuyide jailed 40 years for sexually assaulting 14-year-old girl he was sent to find
stories.p: A US federal judge has sentenced former Kokomo, Indiana, police officer Sinmi Asomuyide, 33, to 40 years in prison for sexually assaulting a 14-year-old runaway girl he met while on duty. DNA found in his patrol car helped prove the case, and investigators uncovered an earlier allegation involving a 15-year-old in Virginia.
body: He was sent to help bring a missing 14-year-old girl home safely. Instead, he became the person who harmed her.

Sinmi Asomuyide, a 33-year-old Nigerian-American former police officer in Kokomo, Indiana, has been sentenced to 40 years in a US federal prison for sexually assaulting the teenager. He will also serve three years of supervised release after his prison term.
## How it happened

On 30 June 2024, the girl's father called the emergency line to report her missing as a runaway. Asomuyide, then on patrol with the Kokomo Police Department, was one of the officers who found her at the home of another underage girl.

While driving her to a youth centre, he switched off his body camera, took her phone and used it to call his own private number. He told her he would contact her later to return an item he had found on her.

Later that evening, after his shift, he went to where she was staying, picked her up while still in uniform, drove her to an empty warehouse car park and sexually assaulted her, according to court documents and GPS data from his car.
## The evidence that exposed him

Asomuyide denied everything. When state police questioned him about a week later, he claimed he had never given the girl his number and that she had contacted him on a work phone, even though Kokomo officers are not issued work phones.
Within hours of the assault, he had also searched online for how to delete the messaging account he used to contact her.
But the evidence caught up with him. Investigators examining his patrol car found a stain on the centre console that matched his DNA.

In June 2026, a federal jury found him guilty after a five-day trial of violating the girl's civil rights by sexually assaulting her while on duty, witness tampering by lying to investigators, and destroying records. The judge handed down the 40-year sentence this month.
## An earlier warning sign
Even more disturbing, investigators found that this was not the first allegation against him.

Before joining the Kokomo police, Asomuyide worked with the Portsmouth Police Department in Virginia. He resigned there after an allegation that he had sexual intercourse with a 15-year-old girl while off duty. When he applied to Kokomo, he gave a false account of why he had left.
## Sworn to protect

The case has shocked many, especially Nigerians at home and abroad. A police officer is trusted to protect the most vulnerable, and a missing child should be safest in the hands of the officer sent to find her.
It also raises hard questions about how a man with a previous allegation involving a minor was able to get another job in law enforcement.
## Over to you
How can someone sworn to protect children become their abuser, and what should police departments do to make sure it never happens again?

stories.h: "If Peter Obi doesn't win in 2027, I'll relocate to Burkina Faso": GehGeh says Obi's supporters back him out of genuine love
stories.p: Social media personality GehGeh says Peter Obi is the only presidential candidate Nigerians support out of genuine love and belief in his ability to lead, and has vowed to leave Nigeria for Burkina Faso if Obi loses in 2027.
body: Popular social media personality GehGeh has declared strong support for Peter Obi ahead of the 2027 presidential election, saying Obi stands apart because of the genuine love and confidence his supporters have in him.
## "Genuine love and belief"
According to GehGeh, many Nigerians backing Obi, the NDC presidential candidate, do so because they believe he is qualified, capable and able to lead the country in a better direction.
He argued that things are different with some other candidates, whose supporters, in his view, are more interested in what they personally stand to gain if their candidate wins.
## The Burkina Faso vow
GehGeh went further, saying that if Obi fails to win in 2027, he will give up on Nigeria completely and relocate to Burkina Faso.
His statement reflects his frustration with the country's political situation and his belief that Nigeria needs a different kind of leadership.
## Different, or just more emotional?

His declaration also raises a fair question. Is support for Obi genuinely different from that for other politicians, or are Nigerians simply becoming more emotionally attached to their preferred candidates? Supporters of every major candidate would argue that their backing is sincere.
## Over to you
Do you agree with GehGeh that Peter Obi enjoys more genuine public support than other presidential hopefuls?

stories.p: The Independent National Electoral Commission has denied claims that its chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, is planning to resign, dismissing the reports ahead of the 2027 general elections.
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has denied claims that its chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, is planning to resign.
## Reports dismissed
The commission dismissed the reports, which had been circulating ahead of the 2027 general elections, and maintained that the chairman is not stepping down.
## Why it matters

Any change at the top of the electoral body this close to a general election would raise serious concerns about preparations for the polls. INEC has faced intense scrutiny in recent weeks, including controversy over AI-generated images in the voter register and growing tension around the "Rig and Die" slogan.
More details are expected as the story develops.

stories.h: Copyright Commission takes legal action against NetNaija, MovieBox over piracy
stories.p: The Nigerian Copyright Commission says it has begun legal action against operators of platforms including NetNaija and MovieBox over alleged copyright violations, warning that sites distributing protected content without permission could be shut down.
body: The Nigerian Copyright Commission (NCC) says it has started legal action against the operators of several online platforms, including NetNaija and MovieBox, over alleged copyright infringement.
## What the commission said

Speaking on Thursday, 12 November 2026, at a copyright sensitisation programme at the University of Ibadan, Barrister Kunle Olatunji, deputy director of the commission's Regulatory and Compliance Department, said the action was part of efforts to protect authors, publishers, filmmakers and other creators whose work is used without permission. He said the Copyright Act 2022 had widened the commission's powers to tackle online piracy, allowing it to seek the closure of entire websites rather than just the removal of individual pirated items.
## Why it matters
Olatunji said the law protects the rights of creative professionals whose works are exploited without their consent.
## Background
The allegations against the platforms have not been tested in court, and their operators had not publicly responded at the time of writing.
more: NetNaija and MovieBox face legal action.
The NCC can now seek to shut down entire sites.
The platforms have not responded.

stories.h: Nkechi Blessing thanks God after nasty bathtub fall in the UK
stories.p: Actress Nkechi Blessing says she narrowly escaped serious injury after slipping in a bathtub while preparing for a photoshoot in the UK, and has thanked God for her recovery.
body: Nollywood actress Nkechi Blessing has shared a frightening experience she had while in the United Kingdom.
## What happened

In a video posted on Instagram on Friday, 13 November 2026, the actress said she had slipped in her bathtub earlier that day while getting ready for a photoshoot. She said she lost her footing, tumbled out of the tub and landed on her back and bottom on the floor. She credited her physical strength for helping her recover quickly, saying the outcome could otherwise have been far worse.
## Her message
In the caption, she thanked God for protecting her and asked her followers to help her give thanks.
## How people reacted
Colleagues and fans flooded her comments with messages of relief and prayers. The actress has been in the news this week after publicly addressing speculation about her love life.

stories.h: Angry residents of Area 1, Abuja, seen destroying posters of President Tinubu and Wike
stories.p: Residents of Area 1 in Abuja have reportedly been seen tearing down and destroying campaign posters bearing the images of President Bola Tinubu and FCT Minister Nyesom Wike. What triggered the anger is not yet clear.
body: Residents of Area 1 in Abuja have reportedly been seen tearing down and destroying posters bearing the images of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and FCT Minister Nyesom Wike.
## What the video shows

Footage from the scene shows a group of young men pulling down large posters mounted on wooden frames by the roadside, ripping them apart and carrying away the torn pieces as onlookers gather near market stalls.
## Why the anger?
The incident has drawn attention, with many asking what could have triggered such an angry reaction.

The exact reason behind the destruction of the posters remains unclear, and no group has claimed responsibility. Even so, it has sparked discussion about public frustration and the relationship between political leaders and ordinary Nigerians as the 2027 elections approach.

stories.h: Presidency denies Tinubu's convoy was attacked after Friday prayers in Abuja
stories.p: The Presidency has dismissed videos shared by ADC chieftain Dino Melaye that purportedly showed youths throwing stones at President Tinubu's convoy after Friday prayers in Abuja, calling them misleading and releasing its own footage.
body: The Presidency has denied claims that President Bola Tinubu's convoy was attacked by stone-throwing youths after he attended Friday prayers in Abuja.
## The claim

Dino Melaye, a chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), shared a video on Friday, 13 November 2026, which he said showed young men throwing stones at a convoy belonging to the President after prayers at the Shagari Central Mosque in Area 1. Voices in the video can be heard chanting a Hausa phrase meaning 'we don't want you'.
## The Presidency's response

O'tega Ogra, the President's senior special assistant on digital engagement and new media, disputed the account on X, describing the videos as misleading and linking them to opposition figures. He released a separate video showing Tinubu leaving the mosque in white attire and a black cap, with supporters waving and taking photographs as he walked to his vehicle. It has not been independently established where or when Melaye's video was recorded.
## Background

The dispute comes amid rising concern about political violence ahead of the 2027 elections. On the same day, the President issued a statement condemning violence at political gatherings, directing security agencies to act firmly against thuggery and insisting that every party must be free to campaign anywhere. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.

stories.h: Portable says he received ₦100 million after campaigning for APC
stories.p: Singer Portable has claimed he woke up to ₦100 million after taking part in campaigning for the APC, without saying who sent it. The claim has drawn criticism online amid economic hardship.
body: Street-pop singer Portable has stirred debate online after claiming he received ₦100 million following his involvement in campaigns for the All Progressives Congress (APC).
## What he said

In a post shared on Friday, 13 November 2026, the singer, whose real name is Habeeb Okikiola, said he simply woke up and found ₦100 million had been paid to him. He did not say who sent the money or what it was for. Earlier reports had linked the payment to an APC governorship candidate in Ogun State, but this has not been confirmed.
## How people reacted
Many social media users criticised the claim, contrasting it with the economic hardship facing ordinary Nigerians and questioning whether celebrity endorsements actually influence voters.
## Background
Portable has openly supported President Bola Tinubu and the APC. The APC has not commented on his claim.
more: Portable says he received ₦100m.

stories.h: "Your approach was inappropriate": South African presidency fires back at Fani-Kayode over livestream complaint
stories.p: South Africa's presidency has accused Nigeria's High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, of misrepresenting what happened when his speech was cut off at the ceremony where he presented his credentials to President Cyril Ramaphosa, describing his public complaint as inappropriate.
body: The South African presidency has criticised Nigeria's High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, over his public complaint that his speech was cut off during the ceremony where he presented his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa.
## Fani-Kayode's complaint
Fani-Kayode had raised concerns about the incident, suggesting that he was interrupted while addressing the gathering during the official diplomatic ceremony.
## South Africa responds

The South African presidency has rejected his account. Responding to the controversy, President Ramaphosa's spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, accused Fani-Kayode of misrepresenting the situation and of wrongly dragging the South African President into a matter that did not require his involvement.
Magwenya also described the Nigerian diplomat's handling of the issue as inappropriate.
## A routine ceremony turned row
The disagreement has drawn attention to what should have been a routine diplomatic ceremony between two African countries.
Diplomatic engagements are usually guided by established protocols, and disagreements over procedure are generally expected to be handled through official channels rather than in public.

For a newly appointed high commissioner, the public exchange has raised questions about diplomatic conduct, and about how misunderstandings between representatives of friendly nations should be resolved.
## Over to you
Was Fani-Kayode right to complain publicly, or should he have handled the matter quietly through diplomatic channels?
more: Fani-Kayode said his speech was cut off at his credentials ceremony.
Ramaphosa's spokesperson said he misrepresented what happened.
